case_name: Shankar Prasad vs Radheshyam And Others
facts_of_case: Devsharan's widow Bhagmaniya Bai executed a Will in favour of the plaintiff. The trial court held that she was not entitled to succeed Devsharan's property. No appeal or cross-objection was preferred by defendant No. 1 questioning this finding. This case came to appeal on two substantial questions of law.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized during the lifetime of a person's first spouse is void.
legal_principles.held: The consequence of a marriage in violation of Section 5(i) of the Act of 1955 has been provided under Section 11 of the Act of 1955 which clearly provides that any marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void and may, on a petition presented by either party thereto, be so declared by a decree of nullity if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5.
cited_cases: Banarsi and Others v. Ram Phal1
Thakumal (Dead) through LRs. Mamtabai & Others v. Chakradhar Rao Bhosle2

legal_principles.principle: A person who marries during the lifetime of their first spouse's lifetime is not entitled to execute a will in favour of another.
legal_principles.held: Since Bhagmaniya Bai would not succeed the property of Devsharan, she was also not entitled to execute the Will in favour of plaintiff.
